parsedVerdict.reasoning: The unit has one file, src/delivery/delivery.module.ts, and it passes. It is a NestJS composition root for one bounded context: delivery, which covers deliverymen and the orders assigned to them. It registers the two related entities in one TypeOrmModule.forFeature([Order, Deliveryman]) call. It declares one controller for each sub-area (DeliverymanController, OrdersController). It provides the repositories and use-case services for those same two sub-areas, and nothing unrelated. The file contains no business rules or invariants, so nothing is duplicated. It also doesn't go around its own abstractions: it wires the dal repositories and services the way Nest expects. One cosmetic point is not a cohesion violation: some service files are named without the '.service' suffix (change-deliverymans-status.ts, find-all-deliverymans.ts). Order-to-deliveryman services such as AddOrderToDeliverymanService and UpdateDeliverymansOrdersService show the two sub-areas are tightly linked, which supports keeping them in one module.
